rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews hid their belief that no book or law was needed after Moses, fearing an explicit claim would stir Arab pride; they instead used a political denial to inflame the Prophet’s opponents.
rows.anchor: Because of this fear, they did not express what they had in their hearts but in order to further inflame his opponents

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an exposes the Jews’ ruse and also answers Quraysh chiefs who arrogantly assumed others could not deserve status and honour.
rows.anchor: Here the Qur’ ān has exposed this prank here and also answered the arrogant Quraysh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jewish statement’s concealed intent was that Moses’ Book and law made any later Book or law unnecessary, a position they feared stating plainly.
rows.anchor: after the Book and the sharī‘ah revealed to Moses (sws), there was no further need of any Book or sharī‘ah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi organizes the response around both the denial’s outward wording and the inner claim hidden behind it.
rows.anchor: both its outward and inward aspect has been kept in consideration

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unlettered people might be excused for denying revelation, but the Jewish inheritors of the prophets and divine Books thereby show that they scarcely know God.
rows.anchor: when this statement is given by people who were the inheritors of all prophets and all Books of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God answers every human need, guidance—the greatest need—cannot be left unanswered; the next page illustrates this with water provided for thirst.
rows.anchor: the God Who has provided an answer to every need found in human beings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God who provides water from earth and sky for human thirst would not withhold guidance; denying revelation shows ignorance of His attributes and blessings.
rows.anchor: He provided them with water from both the earth and the heavens.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks who revealed the Torah to Moses if the Jews’ denial that God revealed anything is true.
rows.anchor: They are questioned that if what they say is really true, then who has revealed the Torah to Moses (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about displaying the Torah page by page expresses the Jews’ ungrateful treatment of God’s Book.
rows.anchor: by saying “which you would show to them page by page” their ungrateful attitude towards the Book of God is expressed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply also rejects the hidden claim that the Torah made later revelation unnecessary: since they concealed that Book, God would not leave people in darkness without fresh guidance.
rows.anchor: why would God have left His creatures wander in darkness and not revealed a fresh guidance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic term translated as sheets or pages is a plural meaning “a writing surface.”
rows.anchor: is the plural of R§ and means “a writing surface.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the Qur’an’s compilation between two covers, the Jews kept the Torah in separately written parts, which made concealment easy for its custodial group.
rows.anchor: They had, on the contrary, divided it into various parts and had written each part separately.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They could hide teachings and prophecies that opposed their interests, concealing most of the Torah from ordinary people and exposing only a smaller part; the Qur’an condemns this grave concealment.
rows.anchor: a greater part of the Torah had been concealed from common people and a lesser one had been exposed to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives guidance and light so people follow the right path rather than conceal it.
rows.anchor: God provides His guidance and light so that people adopt the right path and not that they conceal it.

rows.speaker: Jesus
rows.claim: Jesus, alongside other Israelite prophets, rebuked the concealment of scripture; he taught that a lamp should be placed to illuminate the household and good deeds should be visible.
rows.anchor: Jesus (sws) and some other prophets of the Israelites have rebuked the Israelites for their attitude of hiding parts of the Book of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about being given knowledge unknown to the audience and their forefathers is coordinated with the preceding interrogative sentence.
rows.anchor: The sentence “and you were given that knowledge which neither you nor your forefathers knew” is coordinated to the previous interrogative sentence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After all those favours, claiming that God revealed nothing displays boundless audacity.
rows.anchor: even after knowing all these favours of God, they say that God has not revealed anything, then such audacity has no bounds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers the Jews’ hidden question of why God sent a Book after the Torah and what need it met.
rows.anchor: This verse is an answer to the inward aspect of their statement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the previous verse points out the Torah bearers’ treatment of their Book, this verse explains the Qur’an’s independent status and need.
rows.anchor: The attitude adopted by the bearers of the Torah with it has been secondarily pointed to in the previous verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is not an unannounced book: Abraham received its glad tidings, and Moses and Jesus predicted its arrival.
rows.anchor: its glad tidings were given to Abraham (sws) and its arrival was predicted by both Moses (sws) and Jesus (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mubārak” points to the universal blessing promised to Abraham, fulfilled through Muhammad’s advent from Ishmael’s progeny; Genesis promises blessing to all nations through Abraham’s offspring.
rows.anchor: The former word refers to the glad tiding of universal blessings given to Abraham (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Muṣaddiq” means the Qur’an accords with prophecies in earlier scriptures; Deuteronomy 18 and Gospel chapter 16 describe its characteristics and the need its arrival would meet.
rows.anchor: The word ﻣﺼــﺪق means that the Qur’ ān has come in accordance with the prophecies mentioned about it in previous scriptures.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to warn people around the mother city that rejection of him and the Qur’an will bring a decisive outcome.
rows.anchor: if they do not accept him as God’s messenger and the Qur’ ān as the Book of God, they will face a decisive

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is directed to Quraysh, leaders of the Ishmaelites who lived mainly in Makkah; the Ishmaelites lacked knowledge of prophethood and scripture, and Muhammad’s arrival fulfilled Abraham’s promise of a prophet benefiting all nations.
rows.anchor: The Prophet’s arrival fulfilled this promise.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s established practice is that a nation accepting its messenger becomes a leader among nations, while a nation rejecting him is destroyed after truth is conclusively conveyed.
rows.anchor: if the messenger is accepted by it, then it is installed as the leader of the comity of nations

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s messengers come from their people’s nobles and first address its leaders; Muhammad was born in Makkah, Arabia’s central city and Quraysh’s home, hence Makkah is umm al-qurā.
rows.anchor: For this reason, Makkah is called umm al-qurā.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe in the Hereafter and therefore believe in this Book and guard prayer are the righteous among the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: refer to the righteous among the People of the Book.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi notes that this identification is also discussed in Sūrah al-Baqarah and other Qur’anic verses.
rows.anchor: This topic is also discussed in Sūrah al-Baqarah and in other verses of the Qur’ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage turns from miscreants among the People of the Book to the idolaters of Makkah and briefly recalls their nonsensical remarks.
rows.anchor: After the miscreants among the People of the Book, attention is now directed to the Idolaters of Makah.
